Your goal is to implement the operations required by me or answer the questions proposed by me.
For each of your turns, you should first think about what you should do, and then call exactly one of the provided tools according to the situation.
If you think the output is too long, I will truncate it. The truncated output is not complete. You have to deal with the truncating problem by yourself.
Attention, your bash code should not contain any input operation. Once again, you should use one tool in each turn, and should not respond without function calling.
Prefer short, simple bash commands. Avoid large multi-line scripts unless the task explicitly asks you to create a script or file.
For query tasks, prefer one short read-only command; as soon as shell output contains the exact answer, call answer_action immediately.
For state-change tasks, prefer one minimal change and then one short verification command.
Note that if you think the task has been finished, or there is some message missing to completely complete the task, you should respond with calling the function "finish_action", as no additional information will be provided.
Also, note that if you have gotten the answer to the question, you should call the "answer_action" tool instead of simply writing your answer in your response.
Your answers should be exact and precise (for example, a single number), do not answer with full sentences or phrases.
Always use a tool provided instead of simply responding with content.

Now, I will start a new problem in a new OS. My problem is:

1. Create a temporary directory named "temp_workspace" to hold intermediate files and logs.  
2. Capture a full recursive listing of the filesystem tree rooted at /working and save it to "temp_workspace/tree_snapshot.txt".  
3. From that snapshot, extract all entries whose basename is exactly "workspace" and save them to "temp_workspace/candidate_entries.txt".  
4. For each candidate entry, determine its filesystem type and record entries as "path -> type" in "temp_workspace/entry_types.txt".  
5. Remove any lines in "temp_workspace/entry_types.txt" that denote directories, symbolic links, or special files, leaving only regular-file entries.  
6. De-duplicate the remaining paths and save the result to "temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt".  
7. Verify that each path in "temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt" resides under /working and is accessible, recording any inaccessible paths to "temp_workspace/inaccessible.txt".  
8. If any inaccessible paths were found, log a warning and remove those paths from "temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt", appending actions to "temp_workspace/cleanup.log".  
9. Prepare a final check that will read "temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt" and determine whether to output "yes" if it contains at least one accessible regular file named "workspace", or "no" if it is empty.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

This task mixes implementation and answering. Make the minimal required change first, then verify it, then return the final grounded value/path/output. Avoid oversized diagnostic scripts.

function.arguments:
{"script":"mkdir -p temp_workspace
find /working -print > temp_workspace/tree_snapshot.txt
awk -F/ '$NF == "workspace" {print}' temp_workspace/tree_snapshot.txt > temp_workspace/candidate_entries.txt

> temp_workspace/entry_types.txt
while read -r path; do
    if [ -h "$path" ]; then type="symlink"
    elif [ -d "$path" ]; then type="directory"
    elif [ -f "$path" ]; then type="regular file"
    else type="other"
    fi
    echo "$path -> $type" >> temp_workspace/entry_types.txt
done < temp_workspace/candidate_entries.txt

grep ' -> regular file$' temp_workspace/entry_types.txt > temp_workspace/entry_types_filtered.txt

sed 's/ -> regular file$//' temp_workspace/entry_types_filtered.txt | sort -u > temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt

> temp_workspace/inaccessible.txt
> temp_workspace/cleanup.log
> temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files_clean.txt

while read -r path; do
    if [ -r "$path" ]; then
        echo "$path" >> temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files_clean.txt
    else
        echo "$path" >> temp_workspace/inaccessible.txt
        echo "Removed $path" >> temp_workspace/cleanup.log
    fi
done < temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt

mv temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files_clean.txt temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt

if [ -s temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt ]; then
    echo "yes"
else
    echo "no"
fi
"}
